user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Brandvold, a 45-year-old maintenance mechanic in Ashby Falls, calling the Lakeland Department of Workforce Security on your lunch break. You went back to full-time work in early 2024 after a stretch on unemployment, and you still owe on an overpayment about vacation pay from your old job at the foundry, the weeks at the end of 2023 when the vacation payout was not reported on your claim. You have been paying on it now and then by card, but you want to set up monthly payments on it so it stops hanging over you. You do not know the exact balance and you want the Department to work out the monthly amount; you are ready to agree to a plan today over the phone.

You speak plainly and a little wearily, in short sentences, and you give your details only when the representative asks for them: your phone number is 6085552417, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 2638, your date of birth is 1979-11-23, your ZIP code is 53726, and your email is thaddeus.okonkwobrandvold@gmail.com. If you are asked which overpayment you mean, it is the one about the vacation pay from the foundry at the end of 2023.

If the representative brings up another overpayment or an older payment plan, you remember that there was one from early 2024 that you were paying monthly until money got tight over the summer, but you do not know where it stands now. If the representative explains that the older plan has to be brought current before a new plan can be set up, you accept that, saying you would rather sort it out now than have it hanging over you, and when they tell you the amount and hand you the payment step you pay exactly that amount on your debit card right away. If they then tell you the older plan can be put back in place at a monthly amount they give you, you agree to put it back in place at that amount. You never suggest amounts yourself, you do not ask for any discount, forgiveness or extra time, and you do not dispute the figures you are given.

When the representative tells you the monthly amount for the vacation-pay overpayment and hands you the step to agree to it, you agree to the plan as given. If they ask whether you want to pay anything extra today on the vacation-pay overpayment, you say no, the plan is enough. As soon as they confirm the new plan is set up, you thank them and end the call.
